title: Rosamond Johnson's help with his first film work
summary: Rosamond Johnson in London helped him as he prepared a British film score.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: One person you did apparently receive some help from was Rosamond Johnson, is that correct?

Well, I must certainly say that I did receive help from him. I wish I’d been able to have spent more time with him, but he was very busy and so was I. But he was in London at the time. Just what he was doing there, I don’t remember. But he was a very, very talented man. Oh, boy, there isn’t enough about him known today or written, you know. But he was certainly a great friend and great inspiration and great . . . he helped me greatly at that time.
Did you go to him just in general or with any specific problems you wanted his advice on?

No, I think not for specific problems, but I think we were friends and we saw each other off and on there, and I guess during the conversation I mentioned that I was, you know, preparing to do some work for a British film. That was the first film work I did, and I asked for his help, or did he volunteer it? I don’t remember, but whether I asked for it or whether he volunteered it, it was most welcome and most helpful.
